issue_context.title: DWD Weather Warning Integration: Alerts are not in chronological order and Start/End-Time wrong
issue_context.body:
### The problem

If you have several alerts in the attributes, this are not in chronological order

Example for region_name: 105315000 at 16.02.2022, 22:00 Uhr

```
warning_count: 3
warning_1_name: SCHWERE STURMBÖEN
...
warning_1_start: 2022-02-16T21:00:00+00:00
warning_1_end: 2022-02-17T09:00:00+00:00
...
warning_2_name: STURMBÖEN
warning_2_start: 2022-02-16T08:00:00+00:00
warning_2_end: 2022-02-16T21:00:00+00:00
...
warning_3_name: STURMBÖEN
warning_3_start: 2022-02-17T09:00:00+00:00
warning_3_end: 2022-02-17T17:00:00+00:00
```

In the DWD-Warn-App the warnings are in chronological order on the start date/time

At the example above:

1.) Sturmböen, 16.02.2022, 09:00 Uhr - 16.02.2022, 22:00 Uhr
2.) Schwere Sturmböen, 16.02.2022, 22:00 Uhr - 17.02.2022, 10:00 Uhr
3.) Sturmböen, 17.02.2022, 10:00 Uhr - 17.02.2022, 18:00 Uhr

And you can see, there is an time difference from 1 hour (UTC to UTC+1)

Expected behavior:

Warnings always in chronological order on the start date/time and the time in local german time (UTC+1) because the warnings are always from german.




### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2022.2.7

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Deutscher Wetterdienst (DWD) Weather Warnings

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/dwd_weather_warnings

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
- platform: dwd_weather_warnings
    region_name: 105315000
    name: Warnwetter Köln
```


### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

### Additional information

_No response_

Hey there @runningman84, @stephan192, @hummel95, mind taking a look at this issue as it has been labeled with an integration (`dwd_weather_warnings`) you are listed as a [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L226) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

Hi Gerd,

when I access the entity via the Overview menu, times are displayed correctly for me. 
![Screenshot_20220217-004443](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/15891478/154376466-31609d2f-5461-4acc-a7d9-afe77c0a312d.png)
I think utc time in attributes is pretty standard, the dwd weather forecast component handles times in utc too.

Hi Hummel,

many thanks for your response!

Ok, the UTC time is not the real problem. If the DWD API transmits the start/end time in UTC, then that's the way it is.

But what about sorting?

If there are several warnings, they always arrive in random order.

Sometimes right, sometimes wrong.

This leads to significant problems with automated notifications.

Hi Gerd,

1. about utc:
There are so many pitfalls if timestamps are not utc, e.g. daylight saving time. Timestamps should always be in utc and only in the very, very last step be converted to local time. If you display the timestamps somewhere this is the right place to convert them to local time, but the sensor should always deliver only utc timestamps.

2. about ordering:
Currently the warnings are ordered in the way dwd delivers them. I don't know but the warnings may be orderd by priority first and by time in second place? I don't think dwd adds random to the ordering process.
For sure we can add ordering by time but can we be sure that this is the right usecase for everybody? Must this problem be solved inside the integration or can it, if it is a problem, be solved afterwards?

3. If you want to dig in deeper. The raw data for your area is retrived with the following query:
https://maps.dwd.de/geoserver/dwd/ows?service=WFS&version=2.0.0&request=GetFeature&typeName=dwd%3AWarnungen_Landkreise&CQL_FILTER=GC_WARNCELLID%3D%27105315000%27&OutputFormat=application/json

Dear Stephan,
thank you too for your answer!

UTC is totally fine!
Your and Hummel's statements are completely correct.

Perhaps a note in the documentation would only make sense for a not so fit user.

Regarding "sorting":

The DWD app always sorts by start date/time.

I think that's the correct representation.

I can't explain why the DWD doesn't keep this in their API either.

The problem is automated notifications.

In my opinion, there is no reasonable trigger by which one can recognize that there is a new / changed or omitted message.

Or can you think of a trigger for this?

I therefore go and write a string in a helper entity in the form:

```
{{states.sensor.warnwetter_koln_current_warning_level.attributes.warning_count\
        \ }}-{{as_timestamp(states.sensor.warnwetter_koln_current_warning_level.attributes.warning_1_start)\n\
        \  | int | timestamp_custom(\"%d.%m.%Y %H:%M\")}}-{{as_timestamp(states.sensor.warnwetter_koln_current_warning_level.attributes.warning_1_end)\n\
        \  | int | timestamp_custom(\"%d.%m.%Y %H:%M\")}}-{{ state_attr(\"sensor.warnwetter_koln_current_warning_level\"\
        , \"warning_1_description\") | wordcount }}
```

When I update, I write the previous value to a second helper entity, create a new string based on the new message, and then compare the two helper entities.

Fast and dirty, but so far it's been okay.

However, if the messages always arrive in a different order, then the comparison naturally fails and a message is triggered each time.

But maybe you have a better idea?!

It seems as if DWD orders the warnings by severity first and maybe by time in second place.

Screenshot from their Homepage (App shows the same sorting).
![Harz](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/62512016/154788279-42abb0c6-6156-4402-8d49-3efacf4588d3.jpg)

But when querying the api the sorting is the following:
1. Frost, 2. Glätte, 3. Extreme Orkanböen, 4. Sturmböen, 5. Orkanböen

My proposal:
Order by severity in first place
Order by start time in second place
Same severity and same start time no further distinction/sorting (one can think of e.g. duration)

I agree with your proposal! Maybe add alphabetical sorting as last step so that the order is always identical and reproducible? I also contacted DWD to ask how they are sorting warnings exactly. I'll let you know once I have a response. 

Wouldn't it be only little extra effort to add strict chroncial sorting via config key since you have to change code anyway? Like "If config key set, skip sorting after severity" or so. Thanks again for your effort!

Due to the current weather situation, some reports are coming in.

I regularly checked the order for three warning cells. There is no order :-)
The messages always arrive in random order.

I am therefore curious to see what DWD will say about your request @Hummel95

But regardless of that, I really like the idea of ​​making the sorting configurable.

Maybe you could do it by specifying whether you want "none = no sorting, order according to DWD message" or "severity = sort according to severity and then according to date/time" or " date = sort according to date/time and then according to degree of severity".

What do you think?

For testing i implemented the three sorting options ("none", "severity" and "date") @GerdRuetten described and the results looks good.
But before making a pull-request we should wait what dwd answers and maybe add a fourth option.

Got an answer: 1st sort is for severity, 2nd they were unsure but suspected it's the time that a warning was published so that the most recent warning is at the top.
No further sorting after that.
this answer does not match my results, especially with regard to the degree of severity.  but it doesn't matter, with the three sorting criteria everything should be covered

The information when a warning was issued (raw data value `<effective>`) is currently not provided by the underlying dwdwfsapi. But anyway sorting by the time a warning was published doesn't make sense for me.

The next days i will make a pull-request with the three sorting options from above.

For clarification:
When i'm talking about sorting by **date** i mean sorting by the raw data value `<onset>` = home assistant value `<start>`
When i'm talking about sorting by **severity** i mean sorting by the raw data value `<severity>` = home assistant value `<level>`

Sounds very good!

If you need a Beta-Tester let me know!

I had the same issue when I tried updating another component. I'm now using it through custom components.
With your code already there, it would make sense for the time being to just use it through custom components too (when sorting is required).

> @GerdRuetten sorry for that, but it seems as if you have to life with the current situation.
> 
> 

Yes I understand.  There is nothing you can do.  Nevertheless, thank you very much for your work!

@Hummel95 yes, your right one can still use it as a custom component.

For all interested: You can find the code under https://github.com/stephan192/core/tree/add_sorting_to_dwd_weather_warnings/homeassistant/components/dwd_weather_warnings
The new config parameter is named `sorting`. Allowed values are `none`, `severity` or `date`.

Example configuration:
```
sensor:
  - platform: dwd_weather_warnings
    region_name: 815085370
    name: Warnwetter
    sorting: severity
```

@GerdRuetten i think you can close this issue

Dear Stephan,
dear Hummel,

i fork the integration to custom_components and transmitt your change into it.

Many thanks and have a good day!

Gerd
